result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend two grid modes, keep Record as a separate action, and add undo and a show lock, so they are very close in substance. A has some extra safeguards: undo that restores the live lights, always reopening in Select, and an 'apply to selection' option. However, A cites an unexplained 'skill's rule' and adds generic accessibility points. B ties its reasoning more tightly to show conditions: it stresses that the operator can always see what the next touch will do, lets Paint switch itself off so it can't be left on by accident, and gives a concrete fallback if switching modes proves too slow. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make the same recommendation: two grid modes, Select and Paint, with Record as a separate action that needs confirmation, plus undo and a show lock. B goes further on show-time safety. Its undo restores the actual light levels, not just the screen, it confirms only when a cue would be overwritten, it always reopens in Select, and it weighs the cost it accepts (one extra tap during prep) against a wrong look the audience sees. B has two flaws: a stray reference to 'the skill's rule' and a generic point about accessibility. A is tighter but slightly less thorough, and its idea of reverting Paint to Select 'on a lift' would fight against painting by dragging.
